question: Bhaga and Chandra streams join at which place in Himachal Pradesh forming the river Chenab?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tandi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tandi** is the place in the state of **Himachal Pradesh** where the **Bhaga** and **Chandra** rivers meet to form the **Chenab River**.
 
• The **Bhaga River** originates from the **Bara Lacha Pass**, and the **Chandra River** originates from the **Chandra Taal Lake**.
 
• Tandi is situated in the **Lahaul and Spiti district** of Himachal Pradesh, a region known for its scenic beauty and high-altitude geography.
 
• **Chenab River** is one of the five major rivers of the **Indus River System** and is a significant water source for Northern India.
 
• The confluence of the Bhaga and Chandra at Tandi is of geographical and hydrological importance as it forms the headwaters of the Chenab River.
 
• The Chenab flows through Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir before entering Pakistan, where it merges with the Indus River system.
 
• The location of Tandi is also spiritually significant for the local people, as rivers in India often hold cultural and religious importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhaga and Chandra Rivers:**

 
 
• The **Bhaga River** originates from the **Bara Lacha Pass**, a high-altitude mountain pass in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The **Chandra River** has its source in the **Chandra Taal Lake**, also located in the Lahaul region of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The two rivers traverse through rugged terrains and deep valleys before converging at Tandi.
 
 
 
• **Chenab River:**
 
 
• The Chenab is a **major river** in the **Indus River System**, with significant importance for irrigation and hydropower.
 
• It flows through multiple regions in India and Pakistan, covering a distance of approximately **960 kilometers**.
 
• In Pakistan, it is known as **“Chandrabagha”**, reflecting the combination of the Bhaga and Chandra rivers.
 
• The Chenab plays a pivotal role in the **Indus Waters Treaty**, which governs water-sharing between India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Importance of Tandi:**
 
 
• Tandi serves as a key geographical landmark in Himachal Pradesh, marking the formation of the Chenab River.
 
• The region around Tandi is known for its **high-altitude roads, trekking routes, and scenic landscapes**.
 
• It is also a significant stopover for travelers heading towards **Leh** and other regions in Ladakh.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options in the Question:**

 
 
• **Kullu:** A popular tourist destination in Himachal Pradesh known for its valleys and temples, but not related to the confluence of the Bhaga and Chandra rivers.
 
• **Rohtang Pass:** A high-altitude mountain pass near Manali, famous for its scenic beauty and access to Lahaul and Spiti, but not the confluence point.
 
• **Verinag Spring:** Located in Jammu and Kashmir, it is the source of the Jhelum River, making it unrelated to the Chenab River.
 
 
 
• **Hydrological Significance:**
 
 
• The confluence of rivers like Bhaga and Chandra is a key feature in understanding the hydrology of the region.
 
• Such confluences often have significant ecological and cultural importance in India.
